> 知其雄，守其雌，為天下溪.

Chapter 27 was entirely outward: how to treat people, how to treat things, how to close without a bolt. Chapter 28 turns inward and asks what kind of inner state is required before such a way of acting is possible.

The answer comes as three sentences that are awkward to read: know the male, hold the female; know the white, hold the black; know the glory, hold the disgrace.

Awkward because 知 and 守 are placed together. Know the strong, hold the weak — isn't that "know strength, therefore pretend weakness"?

One character's difference, and two entirely different books. Pretending weakness is strategy. Holding the female is practice.

## Strategy and practice

Strategy has an order: first know, then retreat. You size up the situation, you decide on the lower position, you occupy it deliberately. There is a gap in time between the knowing and the holding, and in that gap is calculation.

Practice has no order: see, and simultaneously do not go there. Not "I know I could dominate, and I choose not to" — that still has the domination in it. Rather: the dominating move is visible and does not get made, without a decision being required.

The three sentences describe the second. That is why 知 is not a preliminary step. You cannot hold the female by not knowing the male; what you would be holding is ignorance, not the valley.

## 溪, 式, 谷

Three positions, and they are not synonyms.

- 溪 — the stream in the valley: low, receiving, and flowing. Water gathers into it because it is lower than everything around.
- 式 — the pattern, the mold: the form by which others are shaped. 知其白，守其黑，為天下式.
- 谷 — the valley, wider than the stream: empty, able to hold, and able to give out.

The progression is from receiving to patterning to holding. And all three share the same mechanic: a position lower than the surrounding terrain.

## The three returns

Each pair ends with a 復歸 — a return.

> 常德不離，復歸於嬰兒.

Constancy of 德 not departing: return to the infant. The infant is not innocence as cuteness; it is the state before positions have been accumulated. Nothing to defend.

> 常德不忒，復歸於無極.

Not deviating: return to the limitless. 極 is a pole, an endpoint; 無極 is the state before an axis has been set. If 白 and 黑 are the poles, 守其黑 returns you to the place where the axis itself is unformed.

> 常德乃足，復歸於樸.

Sufficient: return to the unworked log. 樸 is the timber before the carpenter — which is where the chapter turns to its final image.

## 樸散則為器

When the log is split, it becomes vessels. 器 — the made thing, the utensil, the instrument.

This is not a fall. The chapter does not say the log should have stayed whole. It says: splitting is what produces usable things.

> 聖人用之，則為官長.

The sage uses them — and becomes the one who assigns. Using 器 is not the problem; being used by 器 would be.

## 大制不割

> 故大制不割.

The greatest cutting does not cut.

After three sections about the mind, the last sentence is about the knife. 制 is to fashion, to regulate, to cut to shape. 割 is the actual incision — the separation that makes pieces.

大制不割: the highest form of shaping produces parts without severing them. The log becomes vessels and the log is not denied.

## Why this comes here

Chapter 27 said no one is discarded. Chapter 28 supplies the inner condition for that: a person who has not occupied the high position does not need to divide the world into the worthy and the worthless.

Discarding begins with the axis. Remove the axis — 無極 — and 無棄人 becomes possible rather than aspirational.
